extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to scholarly journals (academic researchers; prospective contributors to Elsevier/Carbon)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors on common reasons editors reject submissions before peer review; focuses on technical, scope, completeness, methodological, clarity, novelty, and interest criteria used in editorial triage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical screening failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Before they even go to the editor-in-chief, articles are checked for technical elements. The main reasons they are rejected are: suspected plagiarism or currently under review at another journal; manuscript not complete (may be lacking key elements such as the title, authors, affiliations, keywords, main text, references and all tables and figures); the English is not sufficient for the peer review process; the figures are not complete or are not clear enough to read; the article does not conform to the Guide for Authors for the journal it is submitted to; references are incomplete or very old.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting plagiarized material or material under review elsewhere (see the journal's ethical guidelines). Ensure the submission package is complete with title, authors, affiliations, keywords, main text, references, and all tables/figures. Have the English language quality sufficient for peer review (use a native speaker or language services if needed). Provide clear, readable, and complete figures. Follow the journal's Guide for Authors and provide up-to-date, complete references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Out of scope (Aims and Scope mismatch)
rubrics_metrics.description: It does not fall within the Aims and Scope — e.g., for Carbon, the material studied may contain carbon, but is not carbon; the study uses a carbon material but the focus is on something different; there is no new carbon science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the journal's Aims and Scope carefully and ensure the central subject, focus, and contribution match the journal's topic and readership; even related-material studies can be out of scope if the focus diverges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete study / not a full paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The article contains observations but is not a full study. It discusses findings in relation to some of the work in the field but ignores other important work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit complete studies with adequate experimental/analytical depth. situate findings comprehensively within the literature (do not ignore important relevant work). Avoid submitting preliminary or fragmentary observations that lack full context, methods, or discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective procedures or data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedures and/or analysis of the data is seen to be defective — e.g., the study lacked clear control groups or other comparison metrics; did not conform to recognized procedures or methodology that can be repeated; the analysis is not statistically valid or does not follow the norms of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established, reproducible methodologies and include appropriate controls/comparisons. Provide statistically valid analyses following field norms. Ensure methods are described with enough detail for replication and that experimental design supports conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions not justified by the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: The conclusions cannot be justified on the basis of the rest of the paper — the arguments are illogical, unstructured or invalid; the data does not support the conclusions; the conclusions ignore large portions of the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build logical, structured arguments that follow from data and analysis. Avoid overclaiming; ensure conclusions are supported by results and engage with the relevant literature rather than ignoring contrary or important work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incremental work / small extension (salami slicing)
rubrics_metrics.description: It's simply a small extension of a different paper, often from the same authors — findings are incremental and do not advance the field; the work is clearly part of a larger study, chopped up to make as many articles as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit work that makes a clear, substantive advance. Avoid slicing one substantial study into multiple marginal papers; demonstrate novelty and significance beyond minor extensions of prior work (including your own).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomprehensible presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: It's incomprehensible — the language, structure, or figures are so poor that the merit can't be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear writing, coherent structure, and legible figures so reviewers and editors can assess scientific merit. Have a native English speaker or professional language service review the manuscript, even if you are a native speaker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of interest / 'boring' work
rubrics_metrics.description: It's boring — it is not archival, is incremental or of marginal interest to the field; the question behind the work is not of interest in the field; the work is not of interest to the readers of the specific journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target questions of significance and readership interest; emphasize archival value and broader impact. If the work is narrowly incremental, consider a different venue or reframe the contribution to highlight novelty and relevance.
